action: Equinor partners and suppliers: no action required yet. Follow Equinor's official updates, treat unexpected emails that appear to come from Equinor with extra care, and confirm payment or access requests by phone.
exec: A major European energy supplier reports a cyberattack on its IT systems has been stopped; operations are reported unaffected.
plain: Norwegian energy company Equinor said on November 17 it had detected a cyberattack on some of its computer systems. TechRadar reports its updated notice says the attack has been stopped, production runs as normal and there is no indication data was stolen.
summary: Equinor said it detected a cyberattack on its IT systems on November 17; production is unaffected and there is no indication data was stolen. On November 18 it saw no risk of the attack spreading and could not say how long restoring would take. TechRadar, relaying Equinor's updated notice, reported on November 20 that the attack was stopped and reported to police. No attacker named.
title: Equinor cyberattack on IT systems stopped, company says; production unaffected

validation.note: Company statement, Reuters, The Record, Cybersecurity Dive and TechRadar (relaying Equinor's updated notice).

review.note: Re-read The Record and Cybersecurity Dive (18 Nov): detected 17 Nov, production unaffected, no indication of data theft, not a virus, restoration time unknown, email down per Reuters via The Record; company statement not opened
